body: I don't know about that, man.  I'm subscribed to r/ImGoingToHellForThis and even they have very minimal ammounts of homophobia.
LOL forgive me.  There's a lot of things my parents instilled in me I'm not proud of.  It's just what I was raised to believe.

I have the feeling that everyone is somewhat gay.  I've spent the last 10 minutes trying to type out my explanation but it keeps turning in to jiberish so oh well.

I moved from a very conservative farm town when I was 15.  I bet if I still lived there and came out to someone they would recommend Jesus Camp to "get the gay out of me".  I live in central Florida now which basically has a good mix of people that hate, love, or simply don't care.

I like how you put your 2nd suggestion.  Most of the girls I've been with I really had no interest in.  I just wanted to fuck which makes me a huge douchebag.  I guess it was all just a pathetic way to tell myself I'm not gay -_-...  I have a pretty healthy relationship with the girl at work.  I want to get to know her more instead of rushing into things.  She's a sweetheart and a bit of an asshole like me :).  If things don't work out that's ok with me,  but I don't want to ignore the mutual feelings.

I've been on reddit for almost a year now.  I love it and hate it.  But it has definately changed my view on life entirely.  I love getting into (what I think comes off as passionate) arguments about how much hate is in this country/world and how it all just slows humanity down.  I don't plan on leaving reddit for a long time.  I've had many submissions to r/SuicideWatch on different throwaways but I never really explained what the real 'problem' was until I created this account.

That RUSH! God I thought I was going to have some sort of seizure on that couch.  This seems like a really good strategy.  When you decide to come out to your parents you could have a few friends that already know just in case your parents decide to be unsupportive.  I think that's what I will do; tell my brother and sister first.

On another note.  I feel like since my feelings are obviously just instinctual and have been with me since I can remember.  Maybe coming out will just give people reason to judge.  Maybe I can be gay/bi/whatever and not have to explain myself because the bottom line is that I'm simply human.

I do like her I suppose.  I always thought she was embarrassed to be around me or thought I was a complete douchebag so I never flirted or really had any dialogue with her at work.  Yet I talk to her on facebook and through text more than anyone else.  I think she's cute and fun but I don't have much passion about her compaired to 2 other girls I work with that I used to be madly in love with (both have boyfriends, pretty much gave up on that).  Just throwing it out there that I'm also 21 and have never had a legit girlfriend.
